definitions.explanation: A wall built by stacking stones, commonly found in castle fortifications, terraced fields, and traditional architecture.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{石垣|いしがき}が{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: The castle's stone walls are beautiful.

examples.japanese: {石垣|いしがき}の{上|うえ}にトカゲがいた。
examples.english: There was a lizard on top of the stone wall.

examples.japanese: {熊本城|くまもとじょう}の{石垣|いしがき}は{地震|じしん}で{大|おお}きな{被害|ひがい}を{受|う}けたが、{修復|しゅうふく}{工事|こうじ}が{進|すす}められている。
examples.english: The stone walls of Kumamoto Castle suffered major damage from the earthquake, but restoration work is ongoing.

notes:
A compound of {石|いし} (stone) and {垣|かき} (fence, wall). One of the most recognizable features of Japanese castles.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{石垣|いしがき} are an iconic element of Japanese castle architecture. The technique of building curved stone walls ({反|そ}り) that slope outward at the base and curve inward at the top was developed to be earthquake-resistant and difficult for attackers to climb. Famous castle stone walls include those at {大阪城|おおさかじょう}, {熊本城|くまもとじょう}, and {姫路城|ひめじじょう}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {石垣|いしがき}を{積|つ}む — to build/stack a stone wall
- {城|しろ}の{石垣|いしがき} — castle stone wall
- {石垣|いしがき}{島|じま} — Ishigaki Island (in Okinawa)

RELATED WORDS:
- {城壁|じょうへき} — castle wall; the broader fortification structure
- {天守閣|てんしゅかく} — castle tower/keep; sits atop the stone walls
- {堀|ほり} — moat; another castle defense feature
